topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic outlines the scope of the lecture and frames the learning outcomes for cancer therapy.

topics.label: Traditional cancer treatment modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the mechanisms, clinical applications, and systemic toxicities of traditional non-targeted cancer treatments including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic approaches that selectively exploit intrinsic genetic, molecular, or signaling vulnerabilities inherent to cancer cells.

topics.label: Oncogene-targeted therapies and kinase inhibitor resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the development, mechanism of action, and subsequent drug resistance challenges associated with therapies targeting driver oncogenes and hyperactive kinases.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how engineered antibodies target tumor cell-surface proteins either to disrupt oncogenic signaling or to selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the immunological basis and modern clinical strategies used to harness, reactivate, or engineer the host immune system to destroy tumor cells.

topics.label: Challenges, progress, and future perspectives in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize long-term historical progress, current translational barriers, and ethical dilemmas shaping the future management of cancer.
